To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the fractionation of human DNA according the its base composition by density gradient ultracentrifugation does not result in a fractionation of DNA according to its sequence composition; and (2) the fractionation does not result, therefore, in a fractionation by sequence class.

the fractionation of human DNA by density gradient centrifugation is not a reliable method to obtain fractions enriched for different sequence classes, but that it is a useful method to obtain fractions of different base compositions that can be used for further study.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible fractionation of human DNA according its base composition.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for a significant fractionation of human DNA into sequence classes according to base composition in the procedures used here.
there are no significant differences in base composition or DNA sequence between fractions of different buoyant density.
no fractionation of human DNA has been achieved to date that would allow the enrichment of specific sequence classes of DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA molecules in each fraction are heterogeneous with respect to base composition and that the fractions are not enriched for any particular sequence class.
the fractionation procedure is not sufficiently specific to be useful for separating different sequence classes in the human genome.
there is no evidence for the existence of a fraction of human DNA which is composed of a single sequence type, or which is enriched in a single sequence type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA of different base composition is not fractionated into different sequence classes, and that DNA of different GC content has similar sequence classes.
the base composition of human DNA is not a useful parameter for fractionation of DNA sequences.
the DNA sequence composition of human cells is not fractionated by density gradient centrifugation.
